minutes.headline: ZBA approved a special permit and variance for new front steps/landing at 102 Pratt Street.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Zoning Board of Appeals heard an application from 102 Pratt Street to remove and enlarge the front steps/landing, which also required a special permit due to intensifying an existing non-conforming front setback. After reading abutter letters of support and questioning the applicant on design and setback distance, the board voted to approve the dimensional relief and special permit with standard conditions, and adjourned.

what_happened.line: ZBA approved a special permit and variance for new front steps and landing at 102 Pratt Street.
The approval carries standard conditions: filing with the town clerk within 14 days, an appeal period, recording at the registry of deeds, and lapse if construction does not begin within two years.
The permit was needed because the new steps intensify an existing non-conforming front setback.
No abutters attended, so the board skipped the public comment period after reading letters of support already on file.

why_it_matters: This is a routine dimensional case for one property, not a policy change, but it shows how the ZBA treats requests that intensify an already non-conforming setback.
Neighbors of other non-conforming lots can look to this decision and its conditions as a reference for what the board expects in similar applications.
The property owner now has fixed deadlines: filing with the clerk within 14 days and starting construction within two years, or the permit lapses.
